description: A three-row step sequencer with a control voltage knob and a gate button on every step, an internal clock, and a clock divider for each row

params.text: Sets the voltage this row's CV output carries while this step is the active one, 0-10V
Switches this step's gate on or off for this row; the lamp beside it is lit while it is on
Sets how many clocks this row takes before moving on a step: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 16, 32, 48 or 64, shown on the display beside it
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before it starts again, 0 to 8; at 0 the module stops and the step lamps go out
Sets the rate of the internal clock, one pulse a second at the bottom of its travel down to one every 0.05 seconds at the top; it does nothing while a cable is in the external clock jack
Switches the gate outputs between Continuous, which holds 10V for as long as that step is the active one, and Trigger, which is a 1ms pulse of 10V as the step arrives

inputs.text: The clock the sequencer runs on; every change from 0V to any other voltage counts as a clock, and patching this jack takes the speed knob out of use
Any change from 0V to another voltage here puts every row back to its first step; clocks arriving in the moment after that are ignored

outputs.text: Passes on the clock the sequencer is running on: the external clock when one is patched, and otherwise the internal clock as a 1ms pulse of 10V
The voltage of the CV knob at this row's active step, 0-10V
The gate of this row's active step, 10V or 0V; a 1ms pulse in Trigger mode and held for the whole step in Continuous mode

notes: with a Sequel Save placed immediately to the right, the whole panel can be saved to four slots and brought back by button or trigger
the three rows share one clock but each has its own divider, so they drift apart and come back together, which is how the polyrhythms are made
a row's CV output is only written while something is patched to it
menu: Randomize all CV knobs — gives every CV knob on the panel a new random voltage
Randomize all gates — turns every gate button on the panel on or off at random
Randomize CV knobs for row 1 — gives the CV knobs of the top row new random voltages
Randomize Gates for row 1 — turns the gate buttons of the top row on or off at random
Randomize CV knobs for row 2 — gives the CV knobs of the middle row new random voltages
Randomize Gates for row 2 — turns the gate buttons of the middle row on or off at random
Randomize CV knobs for row 3 — gives the CV knobs of the bottom row new random voltages
Randomize Gates for row 3 — turns the gate buttons of the bottom row on or off at random
Sample and hold — holds each row's CV output at the voltage it had when that row last fired a gate, instead of following the active step
Use DD cable color scheme - Light — replaces Rack's cable colour list with five colours of the maker's, after a confirmation step; the item ends in Dark under the Rack dark-panel setting

inputs.0:
high above 0V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads the internal clock.
inputs.1:
high above 0V · stepped · one channel only
